claims.claim: Le Guin wrote to Michael Cunningham that when the characteristics of a genre are controlled and insisted upon by publishers, salability, repeatability and expectability replace quality and a literary form degenerates into a formula.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, in conversation with Michael Cunningham, Electric Literature, 1 April 2016

claims.claim: David Naimon writes that Le Guin's political engagement reached down to the defense of language, words and meaning at the sentence level.
claims.source: David Naimon, 'Editing to the End', Literary Hub, 22 May 2018
claims.quote: the defense of language, words, and meaning on the sentence level

claims.claim: David Naimon reports that in talking with Le Guin about craft he quickly learned that everything from sentence length to choice of tense or point of view has a history for her.
claims.source: David Naimon, 'Editing to the End', Literary Hub, 22 May 2018
claims.quote: everything from sentence length, to choice of tense or point

claims.claim: Jason P. Vest names Le Guin's resonant prose as, most of all, what captures the reader.
claims.source: Jason P. Vest, The Common Reader, 30 May 2021

claims.claim: Cummins characterises a character by his diction, saying his nouns, adjectives and metaphors leave no room for ambivalence.
claims.source: Elizabeth Cummins, Understanding Ursula K. Le Guin (1990)
claims.quote: His nouns, adjectives, and metaphors leave no room

claims.claim: Cummins says Le Guin distinguishes the Davidson chapters by his vocabulary, particularly animal metaphors.
claims.source: Elizabeth Cummins, Understanding Ursula K. Le Guin (1990)
claims.quote: distinguishes the Davidson chapters by his vocabulary

claims.claim: That essay credits Le Guin with a flexible use of compound and complex sentences.
claims.source: An essay in Harold Bloom, ed., Ursula K. Le Guin: Modern Critical Views (1986)
claims.quote: a flexible use of compound and complex sentences

claims.claim: Bloom's volume describes Le Guin leading the reader through her alternate realities with a precise, dialectical style.
claims.source: Harold Bloom, Ursula K. Le Guin: Modern Critical Views (Chelsea House, 1986)
claims.quote: her alternate realities with a precise, dialectical style

claims.claim: Cadden says Le Guin uses free indirect discourse to put speakers on a more equal ideological footing with other characters.
claims.source: Mike Cadden, Ursula K. Le Guin Beyond Genre (Routledge, 2005)
claims.quote: put speakers on a more equal ideological footing

claims.claim: Cadden reports that Harold Bloom compliments Le Guin as a writer of precise, dialectical style.
claims.source: Mike Cadden, Ursula K. Le Guin Beyond Genre (Routledge, 2005)
claims.quote: Harold Bloom compliments Le Guin as a writer of

claims.claim: Cadden disputes Bloom's description, saying Le Guin does not seem to value dialectic.
claims.source: Mike Cadden, Ursula K. Le Guin Beyond Genre (Routledge, 2005)
claims.quote: Le Guin does not seem to value dialectic

claims.claim: Attebery says Le Guin has given us a convenient guide to her career.
claims.source: Brian Attebery, The Fantasy Tradition in American Literature: From Irving to Le Guin (Indiana Univ. Press, 1980)
claims.quote: Ursula Le Guin has given us a convenient guide

claims.claim: Petty says one scene is rendered in some of Le Guin's most graphic and moving prose.
claims.source: Anne C. Petty, Dragons of Fantasy (Cold Spring Press, 2004)
claims.quote: some of Le Guin’s most graphic and moving prose

claims.claim: Trimarco's 1999 Journal of Literary Studies article applies a taxonomy of lexical opposition to Le Guin's 'The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas'.
claims.source: Paola Trimarco, "An analysis of lexical opposition: Le Guin's 'the ones who walk away from Omelas'", Journal of Literary Studies 15:3-4 (Dec 1999), 407-424

claims.claim: Kuts and Uholkova say The Left Hand of Darkness is extremely rich in means of artistic expression, among which metaphors stand out.
claims.source: M. O. Kuts and M. I. Uholkova, "Language means of expression while emotional implied sense creation in the works of the 'Hainish cycle' by Ursula K. Le Guin", Intelligence. Personality. Civilization 21:2 (2020), 27-37
claims.quote: extremely rich in means of artistic expression
